pageCache.text:
A place to learn through experience ...
A place to learn about the World...
A place to learn through play...
A place to be creative...
Welcome to Trinity First School. Trinity is a fully inclusive, thriving school where ‘pupils cherish the many memorable learning experiences provided to them,’ Ofsted 2023. We are really proud of our whole school community and love to welcome new members and visitors alike. Please see the School Tours page for details of dates for upcoming tours and Stay and Play sessions for anyone looking for a place for their child to start school in September 2027.
Frome Public Consultation
Over the last 2 years, all key educational stakeholders in Frome have been exploring the possibility of moving to a two-tier education system in the town. Please follow the below link to the Trust’s website to find out more.
https://www.midsomernortonschoolspartnership.com/news/consultation-launched-on-proposed-changes-to-the-education-structures-in-frome.htm
Trinity Church of England VC First School – where we flourish together.
At Trinity First School, it is our mission to nurture and develop the whole child socially, emotionally, intellectually, physically and spiritually to enable them to become the very best that they can be. Through our values of teamwork, curiosity, respect, resilience and kindness we encourage all of our children (and staff!) to embrace challenge; to work independently and as part of a team; to follow their passions; to respect and care for themselves, one another and the world around them and to take an active part in their own learning. We believe in a school community that is full of compassion and free of prejudice. This is embodied in our vision for the school,
‘Encourage one another and build each other up‘.
1 Thessalonians 5:11
Headteacher: Mrs Amanda Seager
Nursery Provision at Trinity
We are thrilled to have added nursery provision to the offer at Trinity First School! The refurbishment of the nursery building was completed in August and we have loved welcoming our first children in September.
If you are interested in finding out more, plesae click here to view the Nursery Page.
Latest News
Welcome back!
We hope you all had a wonderful summer break. We are looking forward to a super Autumn term.

pageCache.text:
About
Trinity First School and Nursery caters for children between the ages of 2 years 8 months and 9 years. We currently have 315 pupils on roll in 11 classes. Our school is set in beautiful grounds on the outskirts of the vibrant Somerset town of Frome. All the children particularly love our wonderful Forest School. Each class visits the Forest School at least once every two weeks. We enjoy close links with the wider community, including the other schools within the Midsomer Norton Schools Partnership Trust, Holy Trinity Church and the other schools within the Frome Learning Partnership. We provide our children with a highly nurturing environment and a broad range of experiences within our school grounds and further afield.
If you are looking for a place for your child to start school in September 2027, we are currently offering parent tours and stay and play sessions for the children. Please see the School Tours page for the dates and links to book or telephone the school office or send us an email to make an appointment.
If you are interested in a place for your child at our nursery, please contact the school office.
For more information, please contact us.

Home » Useful Information » Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care
Our early morning breakfast club,’Kites’, runs from 8.00am Monday –Friday.
The before-school club will open at 8:00am. Upon arrival, children will be offered a glass of milk, juice, or water before engaging in quiet activities such as reading, drawing, or puzzles. Breakfast will be served between 8:00am and 8:20am, consisting of toast with a choice of butter, jam, or Marmite. Parents can drop off their child(ren) at the main hall double doors, located adjacent to the gate from the main car park.
The cost each day for this service is currently £5.00.
Our after school club,‘Trinity Plus’ runs Monday-Friday.
At the end of the school day, children will go straight to the after-school club from their classroom. They will be offered a glass of milk, juice, or water and a biscuit before settling into books, drawing, puzzles, or other organized activities. Older children may choose to use this time to complete their homework. Parents should collect their child(ren) from the main hall double doors, located adjacent to the gate from the main car park. For children staying after 4:00pm, a light tea will be provided. This may include toast, baked beans, fruit, vegetable batons, breadsticks, cheese, hummus, biscuits, or similar options.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Greeting - Trinity CEVC First School : Trinity CEVC First School
pageCache.text:
Home » About » Head’s Greeting
Head’s Greeting
Dear Parents and Carers
Welcome to the website for Trinity First School and Nursery, which is a Church of England VC school sitting in beautiful grounds on the edge of Frome. I have been the Headteacher since September 2015 and I am extremely proud to be leading Trinity First School. As an early years specialist, I know how important it is for children to make the best start possible in their education, and I am especially thrilled that we are now able to offer nursery provision. Our children are happy and friendly here at Trinity. The school day is extremely busy, but there is always a sense of calm and purpose around the school. The warm atmosphere was one of the things that absolutely shone for me when I first visited the school and I know many of our families really value the strong, nurturing relationships that exist between staff and pupils.
We constantly strive to make this school a happy, secure place for children to enjoy success at every level. Our site is spacious, with ten large, light and airy classrooms as well as our newly refurbished nursery. We are blessed with beautiful grounds and have plenty of space for the children to work and play outdoors. There are two separate playground areas, a pond, a Forest School site and an adventure playground in addition to the field we share with Oakfield and Critchill schools. We make use of the outdoors as much as possible because we firmly believe that learning happens everywhere, and the best learning happens when we are actively involved in it.
We teach a broad curriculum, with lots of opportunity for practical, hands-on activities. Our Nursery and Reception children are always busy learning through play and exploration, both indoors and in their wonderful outdoor classroom. Our children continue to follow a play-based curriculum in Year 1 and even into Year 2. Mr Sing is our PE teacher and he teaches each class for one of their two PE lessons every week. During their time at Trinity, the children also have weekly swimming lessons for two terms and we teach them a variety of musical instruments including the violin for our Year 4 children, as well as the ukulele, and percussion instruments for all year groups.
We teach our children early reading using the Read, Write, Inc phonics scheme. We make sure that we invest time and resources into making the teaching of reading as successful as it can be. Alongside secure reading skills, we strive to create a love of reading in our children wherever possible.
At Trinity we like to work with parents in an education partnership. We are proud of the service we offer children and by working with parents we aim to continually improve our offer to your children. Trinity is a nurturing environment in which children are encouraged to do their very best. Their achievements, at whatever level, are recognised and valued. We want our children to love learning and to benefit from the many opportunities a high quality education brings.
I hope our website will help answer lots of questions you may have about life at Trinity School as well as provide a constant source of information for our parents and the wider school community. If you would like to find out more about us, please do contact the school office.
Amanda Seager

Governors
Meet Our School Governors
Below you will find some information about our school governors. For further details, including terms of office for each governor, please refer to the Governor Information document at the bottom of the page.
Chair of Governors – Janice Sledge
I became a parent governor in November 2020 because I was keen to put something back into the school community. I have one child at the school and two who have now moved onto Middle and Upper Schools. In my previous life, before caring for my children full time, I worked in local government. I assisted the Chief Executive, senior managers and councilors to understand the performance of the services they provided to the local community and where improvements needed to be made.
Headteacher – Mrs Amanda Seager
I joined Trinity School in September 2015. I have been a member of the governing body of each of my three former schools, a a teacher, deputy headteacher and headteacher so I can bring a wealth of experience of governance issues. This is my second headship role in a Somerset school, having spent the previous three years as Headteacher at Ditcheat Primary School.
Governor – Rev Ian Snares
I’ve been Vicar of Holy Trinity Church in Frome since 2022, having moved from a church in Hampshire, and joined the Board of Governors at Trinity First School that September. My wife teaches at Frome College where our two teenagers are students. Before becoming a Vicar, I worded as an engineering manager for the Ford Motor Company and have been a trustee of youth work charities. I am keen to build links across our wonderful Frome community, and am excited to see church and school partnering together to provide the best education and care for our children and their families.
Teacher Governor – Mrs Genevieve Mondahl
I joined Trinity as a teacher in September 2018 and have since had two children, with my eldest starting his school journey at a school local to my home this year. I am now going into my second year as staff governor and feel lucky to be the representative for a strong staff team, dedicated to the children’s successful experiences in school and within the community.
Parent Governor – Sam Wray
I became a governor in April 2023. My eldest son is at Trinity, and with my youngest yet to start, I’m likely to be a Trinity Parent for 7 more years. My background is in IT and technology with experience across a range of managerial positions. I have spent a lot of time providing IT services into education, and saw the role of governor as an ideal way to give something back to a school that is doing so much, not just for my son but for the wider Frome community.
Community Governor – Susannah Hanson
I became a Governor in October 2025 . I work for Wiltshire Council in finance for Adult Social Care before that my work roles have been supporting children and young people with complex needs towards independence . I am a Churchwarden at Holy Trinity Church,with whom the school has a flourishing relationship and I live in Frome . I am a Magistrate sitting in the Adult and Youth Courts and am currently the Youth Panel Chair for Avon ,Somerset and Gloucestershire. I am used to working with young people in varied ways and hope to bring my skills to support the school, staff and pupils to the full.
Parent Governor – Alice James
I joined the governors in 2025 as a parent governor and have two children who attend the school. I have also been a primary school teacher for over 14 years and currently teach in Warminster, so have an up-to-date knowledge of policy, curriculum and day-to-day school life. I am passionate about education and community, and am keen to use my experience as both a parent and a teacher to support Trinity.
Parent Governor – Eleanor Butler
With two children loving their time at Trinity, I joined as a Parent Governor in November 2025. Outside of school life I run a public relations consultancy that specialises in a wide variety of sectors, including education and community engagement. As well as a very brief stint as an English Teacher, I have also previously sat on the Board of Trustees of a large regional charity, and so I hope my experience can be of benefit to the school, our community and the children who will remember their time at Trinity as some of the best years of their lives
Clerk to the Governors – Mrs Jane Rose

Home » About » Safeguarding
Safeguarding
Schools are in the frontline when it comes to keeping children safe. Staff in school are trained to follow set procedures when a child discloses information that causes them concern. The School’s ‘Child Protection Policy’ identifies members of staff who have recent and up to date training in all the most effective procedures. At Trinity the Designated Safeguarding Leads are Richard Reid, Amanda Seager and Becca Rutt. Our Child Protection Governor is Alice James. Our curriculum ensures that we teach children about safeguarding, including staying safe online.
Parents need to be aware that if a child discloses information, then we are legally bound to record this information, and we may need to report this concern to Social Care Services. Parents do not always need to be informed by the school when such concerns are recorded or shared. Teachers may well approach parents with concerns over issues such as tiredness, injuries and children reporting lack of food at home. These are not easy conversations to have but it is a school’s duty to share concerns. If you have any concerns about a child, you can contact any of the designated teachers named above.
dsl@trinityschoolfrome.org.uk
Please see our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy for further details.
If you have a concern outside school hours you are welcome to send this to our dedicated safeguarding email address. DSL@trinityschoolfrome.org.uk In the event of an emergency please phone Children Social Care or the police on the numbers listed below.
The Children’s Commissioner has produced a report on safety online for children with some useful advice for parents – ‘How parents and carers can support their children to manage their rights and privacy online’
We were delighted to welcome the NSPCC to one of our recent assemblies. The Speak Out – Stay Safe campaign is wholly supported by the school.
NSPCC also lead the Talk PANTS campaign. This helps children understand that their body belongs to them, and they should tell someone they trust if anything makes them feel upset or worried. See below for more details.
Childline is a national charity available to help anyone under 19 in the UK with any issue they’re going through. You can talk about anything. Whether it’s something big or small, our trained counsellors are here to support you. Childline is free, confidential and available any time, day or night.

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities at Trinity School
At Trinity we know that many children will require extra support during their time spent with us if they are not succeeding quite as well as their peers. This support may be required because they have a previously diagnosed special educational need, medical need, or physical disability. It may be because they need some emotional support. We endeavour to provide the best provision for each child. Provision of additional support, for whatever reason, is reviewed and updated regularly by our SENCo, Mrs Anita Crawley, and training, whether whole-school or for individual TAs, is provided where necessary. Our annual school SEND report provides information about this provision.
Email: sen@trinityschoolfrome.org.uk

Please contact Nathan Williams directly for further information or to book a space. Lessons shall commence from Monday 14th September.
Individual Piano Lessons (Ukulele / guitar also possible on request)
Piano lessons are individual and delivered in the staff room on Monday afternoons during school time, charged at £10 for 15 minutes. All lessons are payable half termly, in advance. Individual guitar/ukulele lessons may also be available should timings allow. Nathan has a great deal of experience working with children of all abilities and needs. Please contact Nathan Williams directly for further information or to book a space. Lessons shall commence from Monday 14th September.
Trinity Brass – Individual lessons (Y2+)
When: Tuesday afternoons during school time
Who to contact: Roy Dignum daddydiggers@icloud.com
Roy Dignum can teach trumpet, cornet, tenor horn and trombone offering a 15 minute 1:1 lesson every Tuesday afternoon for £9 a lesson (paid every term). To support our families, I have negotiated with All Instruments (Westbury) to hire brass instruments out for £12 every full term. They will knock the hire charges off any instrument purchased later down the line. Please contact Roy directly to book, he currently has 2 remaining slots available. Roy is CRB checked and is extremely kind and offers a supportive learning environment. This opportunity would be best suited from year 2 upwards. Lessons shall commence on Tuesday 8th September 2026.
Trinity Brass band is held after school in Chestnut class at 3.20pm until 4.00pm. Rehearsals are free of charge for ALL brass musicians. Please contact Roy directly for further information or to book a space. The first rehearsal shall commence on Tuesday 8th September 2026.
African Drumming & Dance Club
This club runs after school in Chestnut class on Mondays 3:15pm – 4:00pm with Abi Bailey. Abi is a professional teacher who is engaging and brilliant! Trinity First School has 15 full size djembes and 15 small djembes on site so you do not need to provide any equipment for your child to participate. Lessons are charged at £4 per session chargeable per half-term. To book on please contact Abi with your child’s class and details to djembetots@gmail.com The children are dismissed through the top gate by Chestnut class at the end of the session. Lessons shall commence from Monday 14th September.
A fun, free of charge choir where the children can learn songs and key choral skills.. Children from Year 1 upwards are welcome to attend. (Sunshine and Rainbow children are welcome to apply in the summer term.) Rehearsals are held in the Chestnut classroom and children will be dismissed through the main gate at the end of each session. If your child would like to join ‘Songbirds’, please either complete the reply slip (emailed out at the beginning of term via parentpay) or send a note with your child’s name, year group and class name and hand to your child’s class teacher addressed for the attention of Mrs Williams by Monday 14th September. Please note that we are starting a fresh register, so you will need to re-apply even if your child attended last year. Rehearsals shall commence on Wednesday 16th September.

Curriculum
At Trinity First School, we offer our children a creative curriculum which provides many opportunities to learn and develop skills. Our curriculum reflects our understanding that learning is interconnected and that all children have different skills and abilities. We recognise and value that our children love different things and learn in different ways. Lessons are carefully planned to build on existing knowledge and experiences to make learning relevant to the children. Our children are also encouraged and supported to approach new learning with confidence and to embrace challenges. Please click on the links to see the curriculum overview for each year group and the subject specific overviews. If you would like to know more, please speak to your child’s class teacher or contact the school via the school office.
We use the Read, Write, Inc scheme to teach our children phonics and early reading skills in Reception and Key Stage 1.
Parental right to withdraw children from R&W
Parents have the right to choose whether to withdraw their child from R&W without influence from the school, although a school should ensure parents or carers are informed of this right and are aware of the educational objectives and content of the RE curriculum. If pupils are withdrawn from R&W, schools have a duty to supervise them, though not to provide additional teaching or to incur extra cost.

Reception (Rainbow & Sunshine)
Welcome to the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS).
The staff of Sunshine and Rainbow Class are delighted to share with you information about the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS).
Sunshine Teachers
Mrs Sandquest (Monday & Tuesday) and Mrs Griffin (Wednesday – Friday)
Rainbow Teachers
Mrs Wheeler (Monday – Wednesday) and Miss Draws (Thursday & Friday)
Teaching Assistants
Hayley Fry, Lorna Kirtley, Lissa Young, Chris Cantrell and Sarah Watkins work across the Early Years unit.
The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum has seven key areas of learning.
WHAT TO EXPECT IN THE EYFS – GUIDE FOR PARENTS
The children learn through play based activities, both indoors and outdoors. We work closely as a unit and the children can free flow between the classrooms and the outdoor area. We also use the school grounds and local area to support our learning.
At the beginning of the year, your child will participate in the Reception Baseline Assessment (RBA). At the end of the year, your child will be assessed against the Early Learning Goals.
Early Learning Goals overview for parents
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Expressive Arts and Design
Important information
This term our outdoor adventures will be on Tuesdays.
We use Read, Write, Inc. (RWI) to teach phonics. We hold a Read, Write, Inc. parent information session in Term 1, but if you have any questions about the scheme or supporting your child, please ask.
For more information about Read, Write, Inc., please click the link.
Please listen to your child read every night and make a comment in their reading record. We use the children’s reading book in class daily, so please ensure that it is packed in your child’s book bag ready.
Our library day will be on a Monday. The children can choose between fiction and non-fiction books. These books are for you to share with your child at home. Please ensure that your child brings their library book in on a Monday to change.
PE with Mr Sing is on a Wednesday. Children need to come into school wearing their PE kit on this day.
Your child will also be involved in lots of other physical opportunities throughout the week. Some of these include: balance bikes, scooters, trim trail, yoga and playground games.
We use Class Dojo as our main way of communicating with parents and carers. We will put messages and reminders on Dojo, so please check this regularly. You can send us messages on Dojo too, but we may not see messages during the school day. If your child is going home with someone else, please phone the school office.
We also use Dojo to post photographs of some of the activities that we are doing at school. We love to see the things that your child is doing at home, so please do share their activities and learning.
We are always looking for extra helpers in school. If you are interested in helping, please contact the school office.
